question: Which was the first ancient Indian civilization that had systematic town planning and underground drainage systems?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Indus Valley civilization.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indus Valley civilization is one of the earliest civilizations in the world and flourished around 2600 BCE.**
 
• The Indus Valley civilization was notable for its advanced town planning**, which included well-organized streets, drainage systems, and public buildings.**
 
• The ancient cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro in the Indus Valley region had well-planned streets, public baths, and underground drainage systems ahead of their time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Nubian civilization** refers to the civilization that emerged in the **Nile Valley around 2000 BCE.** Still, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems in this civilization.
 
• **Later Vedic civilization **refers to the period of Indian history tha**t followed the decline of the Indus Valley civilization,** and while this period saw the emergence of the caste system and the Vedas, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems.
 
• **Aegean civilization** refers to the civilizations that emerged in the Aegean region, including the Minoan and Mycenaean civilizations, but while these civilizations had impressive art and architecture, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems.
